title: Meta parts ways with Virtue AI
key_facts: Meta is letting go of employees it hired from the AI safety startup Virtue AI, four months after they joined in June.
Meta spokesperson Andy Stone told Semafor the arrangement 'didn't work out as planned'; Semafor says he chalked it up to clashing work styles.
Stone said Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.
Virtue AI is an AI security startup that had worked with Anthropic, OpenAI and the Commerce Department's NIST.
Axios reported in June that co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song and Sanmi Koyejo were joining Meta along with other Virtue employees.
Semafor says the team did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Semafor's own view is that the departures show Meta is still shaping its AI and AI safety strategy amid new calls for regulation in Washington.
quote_evidence: Meta said it's letting go of employees it hired from AI safety startup Virtue AI four months after they joined the company in June, Meta spokesperson Andy Stone told Semafor, chalking it up to clashing work styles.
"Unfortunately, the arrangement didn't work out as planned," Stone said, adding that Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.
Axios reported in June that Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song, and Sanmi Koyejo were joining Meta along with other employees from the startup.
why_it_matters_hint: Meta says its AI safety work continues, but a team it hired only four months ago is leaving.
event_date: 2 Oct 2026 (Semafor); the hires were in June 2026.
notes: Short article. It does not say how many people are affected or whether the three co-founders are among them.
